Hey, I'm a bit new here. I've been hanging out at /r/asatru since 2011ish (I think) under a different name and wanted to see if there was an equivalent place over here. Seems a bit slow. So how about an intro thread to spark some ongoing discussion. Itll also help me test a theory about whether or not the subreddit is as insular as I think it MIGHT be. (not in a bad way, per se. Just sociological curiosity) So heres my questions for you: I can already see your name, so how old are you? Whereabouts do you hail from? What kind of heathen are you? However you want to answer that. Universalist. Folkish. Tyrsman. AFA. Troth. Undecided. Atheist (we saw a few of those over at /r/ recently). Trans-Hindu. Crazy bearded man living on a mountain. Whatever. Do you have a Kindred? Do you have any strong feelings about them? Do you heathen alone? With family, friends, kindred? What are you doing? Reading dat edda? trying to practice every holiday the AFA recognizes? Donating time to build McNallens Hof? Browbeating the lokeans? Brag about something. Tell me something you are super proud of. We're heathens, boasting is in the culture. Any part of Heathenry you dislike and would rather change? Do you have a view of the heathen cosmology that you would like to share?

I had some health issues for the past weeks and wasn't able to check voat. The sub is slow, true, but nevertheless it's usually more alive than last couple of weeks :) I think the biggest difference between /v/asatru and /r/asatru is that we're extremely open minded and welcome other views (even those we don't agree with), where /r/asatru is very USA/recon based and I see people getting downvoted for having other opinions/type of heathenry

I'm from the Netherlands and I don't like all these cute little heathen categories that people come up with, but if anything I believe everyone has the right to practice and everyone has the right to their own personal interpretation. It doesn't affect me personally in any way if someone wants to worrship some giant that is mentioned somewhere in a register. Go right ahead. I don't understand why most people get bothered about those things. (Please, do explain)

I have a kindred, people who I've known for many years, we split off from the Netherlands Heathenry group, which is heavy on the academics and recon. The reason we left was because the only focus there was academics. We prefer to experience some spirituality with our heathenry, which was impossible for me in the previous group because doing rituals were just empty gestures based on what was in some book. I think research and experience need to be in balance and I think it's healthy to ask yourself why you are doing a ritual in a certain way, and not "because we are supposed to". (and there were some issues with untransparent leadership and decisionmaking)

The kindred really is the keystone to heathenry in my opinion. I guess I'd describe my kindred as chosen family. Aunts and uncle type of relationship. You don't get along with everyone equally but they are still a part of my kindred so it's pretty limitless what I would do for them. We celebrate holidays together, like any family would. We work on a democratic base too: if anyone wants to organise an event or lead a ritual, it's about taking the initiative to do so. There's no gothi's or heads of the family or whatever people come up with. We have a thing twice a year in which we talk trough most decision making and people can discuss things that bother them and we make plans for gatherings. Everything we do and organise is completely transparent and open for input from others

The important holidays get celebrated with the kindred and besides that I also "heathen alone" as you say, in the regard that I use seidh and communicate with the ancestors and land spirits, and the gods are in there somewhere too. I don't think that heathenry is something that you do as a verb, it's rather a worldview.

My research pretty much focusses on the dutch gods and folklore, because most stuff on heathenry focusses on the scandanavian gods. Wodan, Donar, Nehalennia, Vrouw Holle etc. Besides that I organise events like celebrations, museum visits and such and I help people that are new to heathenry in the netherlands to find a kindred that suits their views, attend meetings with other kindreds and heathens and all that jazz. It's a pretty social culture in northern europe, we have contacts in scandinavia, belgium and germany and it's all in good fun.

Anything else I want to share? Hmm. I think heathenry in northern Europe is very distinct from the USA. I guess it's the difference that most groups here are focussing more on their experience and spirituality, and feed those things with their research, while in the states most people rely very heavily on the academics and pass by the spiritual part because there's a lack of logic and proof. I think it's a bit of the revivalist vs reconstruction idea.

"Any part of Heathenry you dislike and would rather change?" Hmm It's not that I dislike wicca-bent rokkatru or academicism, I just don't see it as what heathenry is to me. However, it's not my place to say it isn't heathenry at all or should be changed. Like I said before, it doesn't really affect me, so why get bothered by it? If I want to change something thats kindred-related I just discuss it in the thing and it might get changed or someone might be able to change my mind. Has never been a problem so far.

Come to think of it, however, If I had the power to change heathenry, I'd kick out all the bigots who are opposed to gay marriage or say you need to be from germanic blood to be heathen. Ah, and I'll kick out all the viking-wannabe's too (What do you mean "listening to amon amarth doesn't make me heathen?") Hey, this kicking people out thing is easy! Alright, alright, I'll kick out all wicca-bent roccatru and acadamists out too and start my own dictatorship of love and equality. NOW HUG EACHOTHER OR I'LL HAVE YOUR HEAD!

"Do you have a view of the heathen cosmology that you would like to share?" I think the hierarchy of importance in heathenry is: 1. your family 2. the rest of the kindred, 3. the ancestors, 4. land spirits and 5. the gods, I usually see people who adapted the christion/medieval vision of god-is-on-top-of-the-world and basically adapt to a form of christianity with a veil of vikingness.
